title: zBox Package Catalog
description: Schema for the curated package list consumed by zBoxTUI's Configure Packages dialog. Lives alongside packages.json so the catalog repo can CI-validate PRs.

schema_version.description: Bumped when the schema changes in a way that breaks older clients. Clients should refuse to load catalogs with a schema_version they don't understand.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the catalog was last refreshed (typically set by the catalog repo's bump-versions CI).

name.description: Group label shown in the picker as [ name ].

description.description: Optional one-liner explaining what this group is for. Not rendered today; kept so the file documents itself.

package.description: A curated package. The `type` field picks which install path applies.

name.description: The Debian package name passed to apt-get.

locked.description: If true, the user can't uncheck this row — the package is always installed when present in the catalog.

name.description: Display name; also used as the cache/state key.

version.description: Currently-pinned version (no `v` prefix). The catalog repo's bump-versions CI keeps this fresh by polling the GitHub Releases API.

github_repo.description: owner/repo on GitHub. Used by catalog CI to discover new releases.

binary.description: Path of the installed binary. Used to detect presence quickly when `version_command` isn't set.

version_command.description: Shell command that emits the installed version. zBoxTUI runs it and captures the first match group of `version_pattern`.

version_pattern.description: Python `re` regex with one capture group, applied to `version_command` output to extract the installed version.

install_command.description: Shell command run as root to install or upgrade. `{version}` is substituted from the `version` field.

uninstall_command.description: Shell command run as root to remove the package.

version.description: Latest known version. May be a placeholder when the install script always pulls latest; bump manually as you validate new releases.

install_command.description: Shell command run as root to install. `{version}` is substituted when present.
